content.text: {"headline":"Recommended: no action (P0) — predicted 83.1% service level for 11:30-19:45 at no extra cost, but payments alone sits just under target at 79.7%.","why":"Payments calls are running well above forecast (+59% at 11:15, 124 vs 78.1) with no explanation in the feeds. Staffing and handle time match plan, so this is a demand problem. Even so, the model predicts the combined service level recovers to 83.1% over the disruption window (rest of day 83.3%) with a 4.5% abandon rate. That clears the 80% target without spending anything or moving people. P0 was chosen as the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches target.","trade_offs":["Payments customers carry the risk. Their queue is predicted at 79.7%, just under 80%, while general is at 89.3%. The target is met on the combined figure, not by both queues.","P1 (free levers: callback, break delay, cross-skilled moves) also costs nothing but predicts worse results: 80.3% overall, payments 75.9%, abandon 5.0%. It also pulls agents off general (down to 88.2%).","P2 (chat deflection plus callback) reaches 87.9% (payments 85.5%) with abandon at 3.1% for INR 1,560. This is the cheapest way to get a real margin on payments if you are uneasy about the forecast.","P4 (partial overtime plus free levers) gives the best result: 92.4% overall, payments 90.6%, abandon 2.2%, for INR 6,516. P3 (full overtime) costs more at INR 7,920 and delivers less (90.8%)."],"watch":"The surge cause is unknown and was still growing at the last reading. If payments volume keeps climbing or payments service level stays below 80% over the next couple of intervals, switch to P2 (INR 1,560) or P4. Recheck the incident and campaign feeds for a source."}
